newsitem.title: USA: Novartis to cut 205 U.S. jobs, close some plants.
newsitem.headline: Novartis to cut 205 U.S. jobs, close some plants.

text.p: Novartis, the Swiss drug firm that resulted from the merger of Sandoz AG and Ciba-Geigy AG, said Thursday it would cut 205 jobs of its U.S. workforce and close some plants in a bid to streamline its national health care manufacturing operation.

"The merger of Ciba and Sandoz results in a duplication in resources and provides an opportunity for Novartis to consolidate health care manufacturing and distribution facilities into a more streamlined, cost effective system," said Doug Watson, the designated U.S. Chief Executive Officer of Novartis.
The company said its U.S. health care business employs 2,295 people.
It said that some Ciba and Sandoz facilities would be closed over the next five years, including plants in Summit, N.J. and Fort Washington, Pa.
